You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
A patient with a history of asthma and transient pulmonary nodules has undergone a chest X-ray (Figure 3) during corticosteroid treatment. The clinical history suggests the presence of Churg-Strauss syndrome. Which of the following findings is most consistent with the expected presentation on the chest X-ray during corticosteroid treatment?

A) Cavitated nodular density in the left lower lobe.
B) Complete absence of pulmonary nodules.
C) Confluent opacities in the right upper lobe.
D) Multiple small nodular opacities with irregular margins.
E) Ground-glass opacities in the left upper lobe.
F) Evidence of lymphadenopathy in the mediastinum.
